referees.quote: my main concern is the use of defect-engineered VO2 film may affect its novelty and significance... it is difficult to say assess to what extent the same physics would also apply to pristine VO2 films.
I have, however, several concerns that the authors must conclusively address before the validity and scientific utility of the work are sufficiently clear to merit publication

note: The first round is Version 0 in this file; there is no sign of a transfer from another journal, and no referee co-signs another's report. Neither referee states a recommendation, so both are inferred. R1 is the borderline case. They call the work interesting and the conclusions generally well supported, which could suggest minor revision. But their central concern questions the work's significance and whether it applies to pristine VO2, and they ask for an overstated claim to be revised. Addressing this required substantial new material: the authors added pristine-device data in the SI and new Discussion text. So R1 is rated major revision. R2 asks for substantial new data and analysis: representative diffraction patterns, ruling out mosaicity, a quantitative estimate of current-induced heating, and apparatus stability tests. That is a clear major revision.
